chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 294: Li Huowang swallows Black Tai Sui – aftermath horror
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang survives the Zuowandao fight but faces a worse enemy: his own mind. Chun Xiaoman ages years. And that Black Tai Sui? He forces it back down.
og_title: After the Battle, the Real Horror Begins – Ch. 294
og_description: Li Huowang survives the Zuowandao—only to swallow his own parasitic tentacles. The cost of victory is measured in years, blood, and a crowded skull.
twitter_title: He ate the Black Tai Sui. On purpose.
twitter_description: Li Huowang survives the Zuowandao fight, but his own hallucinations are getting worse. Also: Gouwa’s coffin hustle.

lore_anchors.definition: A grotesque parasitic entity produced by twisted cultivation; in this chapter, Li Huowang forces it back into his body because it suppresses his hallucinations, treating it as a functional survival tool rather than a poison.
A consumable alchemical item that grants additional years of life; Li Huowang offers them to Chun Xiaoman to reverse the aging caused by excessive Wandering Lord summoning.

A government-sponsored bureau that polices supernatural activity; Li Huowang believes joining them will give him protection and access to proper cultivation methods, framing it as his only hope for stability.
A wandering spirit or entity summoned for alchemy and combat; each summoning costs months of the user’s lifespan, and four summons cost a full year.
A folk trick used to simulate tears by irritating the eyes; Gouwa uses it to fake grief, underscoring his transactional, pragmatic approach to mourning.
